en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Turning Back, 37.
The Training Rule on Another Kingdom:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were wandering on tour within their own country, which was considered dangerous and fearful, without a caravan of travelers.
Rogue men violated them.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before] ...were indignant, complained, and grumbled, saying:
“How indeed can bhikkhunīs wander on tour within their own country when it is considered dangerous and fearful, and they are without a caravan?
… “Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs are wandering on tour within their own country when it is considered dangerous and fearful, and they are without a caravan?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How, monks, can these bhikkhunīs go on tour within their own country when it is considered dangerous and fearful, and they are without a caravan?
This, monks, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence…” [and so forth].
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule:

“If any nun should travel on a journey within her own country where it is considered risky and dangerous, without being accompanied by a caravan, she commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
“Any nun who... means:
Whichever [nun] of such a kind...
"a bhikkhunī"...
this is the bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"In the kingdom of Antora" means in the kingdom of the one in whose realm he dwells.
"Perilous" (sāsaṅka) means:
On that road, the place where the bandits had encamped is seen; the place where they had eaten is seen; the place where they had stood is seen; the place where they had sat is seen;
the place where they had lain down is seen. That road is called "perilous" because people are seen there who have been killed by the bandits, robbed, and beaten.
"Without a caravan" means without a company of travelers.
"She should go on a journey" means...
In a village where a cock can fly from one house to another, there is an offense of expiation for every interval between houses.
In a forest region where there are no villages, there is an offense of expiation for every half-yojana.
There is no offense—
He travels with a caravan,
he travels in safety and without fear,
and in times of calamity.
"Against one who is insane," "against one who is a first-offender.
The seventh training rule is concluded.
